major_concerns: Simulator fidelity vs real vendor behavior may bias operational-failure labels.
Deterministic verifier may have vendor-specific blind spots, confounding method comparison.
Synthetic topology and vendor templates risk limited external validity and licensing/privacy issues.
required_design_repairs: Validate simulator/emulator on small set of vendor reference configs and report gaps.
Specify verifier capabilities and limitations per vendor; log verifier detection taxonomy.
Sanitize vendor templates for licensing and document provenance; expand vendor diversity or justify selection.
Pre-register exact prompt templates, seeds, retry policy, and model-call budget; include paired-baseline enforcement.

major_concerns: Adversarial payload creation raises ethical/security risks and reuse potential.
Definition and operationalization of 'poisoned retrieval' and sanitization heuristics are underspecified.
Containment and non-public release of adversarial artifacts required for safety/compliance.
required_design_repairs: Add an ethics/containment plan; restrict distribution and label adversarial artifacts securely.
Precisely define retrieval pipeline, poisoning rules, and sanitization algorithms; preregister them.
Include a non-adversarial model-only baseline and measure retrieval contamination rates.
Report false-positive costs of sanitization and operational tradeoffs.

major_concerns: Simulator-derived safety labels may imperfectly map to operational impact (construct validity).
Benchmark sampling could bias metric comparisons toward verifier strengths.
Releasing artifacts may implicate vendor licensing or sensitive configuration fragments.
required_design_repairs: Define and justify simulator safety-severity mapping and validate on held-out examples.
Prespecify sampling strategy to avoid selection bias; stratify by task type and topology size.
Sanitize released artifacts and include provenance/licensing metadata; consider synthetic alternatives.
Compare verifier-metrics against multiple surface metrics and across at least two LLMs for robustness.

major_concerns: Human-in-the-loop results rest on simulated operator models whose realism is uncertain.
Policy recommendations risk misguidance if operator-model parameters are mis-specified.
No human-subject validation reduces external validity for operator workload and override behavior.
required_design_repairs: Ground operator-simulator parameters in cited empirical studies or telemetry; preregister parameter ranges.
Run extensive sensitivity analyses and report regimes where conclusions reverse.
Be explicit that findings are conditional on simulator assumptions; avoid prescriptive guidance without human validation.
If possible, incorporate small real-operator calibration (public datasets or prior studies) to anchor simulator.

major_concerns: Curating a reliable, balanced labeled fault corpus is labor-intensive and prone to label noise.
Some semantic faults may be inherently undecidable for deterministic verifiers; expectations must be bounded.
Augmentations may inflate false-positives and operational friction; tradeoffs must be quantified.
required_design_repairs: Provide detailed taxonomy with labeling guidelines and inter-annotator agreement targets; preregister adjudication rules.
Quantify computational overhead of augmentations and measure precision/recall tradeoffs.
Report which fault classes are provably undecidable or practically undetectable and adjust claims accordingly.
Ensure reproducibility by publishing sanitized examples, verifier code, and annotation artifacts.
